sources.title: Euler V1 exploit and recovery historical account
claims: Euler V1 was exploited on 2023-03-13 for approximately $197 million in assets.
The exploit cause was a missing account health check in donateToReserves.
The attacker donated collateral to become liquidatable and self-liquidated to capture a liquidation bonus greater than the donation loss.
The first exploit transaction occurred at approximately 08:50:59 UTC and extracted roughly $8.8 million before later exploit transactions drained additional assets.
limitations: Published after the incident and recovery; use the linked onchain transaction for exact transaction identity and block facts.

sources.title: Euler first DAI exploit transaction
claims: The transaction succeeded on Ethereum at block 16817996.
The transaction flash-borrowed 30,000,000 DAI from Aave V2 and interacted with Euler Exploit Contract 1.
The transaction is the first exploit transaction linked by Euler's official historical account.
limitations: This is one representative exploit transaction from a multi-transaction, multi-asset incident.

sources.title: Euler Finance Incident Post-Mortem
claims: The exploited vulnerability stemmed from donations being possible without a proper account health check.
The vulnerable behavior was introduced with the donateToReserves feature in eIP-14 and interacted with Euler liquidation logic.
limitations: Security-firm technical analysis; exact transaction state remains anchored to the onchain source.

sources.title: Verified Euler V1 main contract source
claims: 0x27182842E098f60e3D576794A5bFFb0777E025d3 is the verified Euler V1 main storage/dispatch contract on Ethereum.
Verified source identifies the contract name as Euler Protocol and exposes the protocol module dispatch architecture.
limitations: The vulnerable donateToReserves behavior executes through Euler's modular/proxy architecture; the main contract address is recorded as the stable affected protocol anchor rather than claiming it alone contains every vulnerable implementation line.
